question: Which among the following NOT a pharmacological action of opioids
analysis: Opioids are well-known for their ability to suppress cough, induce miosis (pupil constriction), and cause truncal rigidity (muscle stiffness). These are common pharmacological actions associated with opioid use. However, anti-emesis (preventing vomiting) is not typically a pharmacological action of opioids. In fact, opioids are more commonly associated with causing nausea and vomiting as a side effect rather than preventing it. Therefore, the action of anti-emesis is not aligned with the typical pharmacological profile of opioids.
